chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was a man during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called Dhū al-Namirah, and he was among the ugliest of people, and he was named Dhū al-Namirah because of his ugliness. So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon me.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Allah has made obligatory upon you seventeen cycles of prayer during the day and night, fasting the month of Ramadan when you reach it, Hajj when you are able to find a way to it, and Zakat,' and He detailed these for him.

He said, 'By the One Who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I will not add anything to my Lord beyond what He has made obligatory upon me.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'And why, O Dhū al-Namirah?' He said, 'Because He created me as ugly.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'So Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your Lord commands you to convey greetings to Dhū al-Namirah from Him and to say to him: Your Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says to you: 'Would you not be pleased that I resurrect you upon the beauty of Gabriel (peace be upon him) on the Day of Resurrection?''

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'O Dhū al-Namirah, this is Gabriel commanding me to convey greetings to you and your Lord says to you: 'Would you not be pleased that I resurrect you upon the beauty of Gabriel?'' So Dhū al-Namirah said, 'I am indeed pleased, O Lord. By Your Honor, I will surely increase (in worship) for You until You are pleased.'

key_terms.ذُو النَّمِرَةِ: Dhū al-Namirah (The Man of the Leopard Skin/Ugly Face), a companion known for his ugliness
key_terms.صَوْمَ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Dhū al-Namirah and his interaction with the Prophet regarding his ugliness and worship?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, the companion Dhū al-Namirah, known for his physical ugliness, inquires about his obligatory duties and initially accepts them without addition, citing his appearance as a reason for contentment. However, upon receiving Gabriel’s divine promise of resurrection with the beauty of the Archangel, he vows to increase his worship beyond the minimum to attain divine pleasure. This hadith is often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the virtue of voluntary devotion (nafl) and the spiritual transformation of character through divine grace.
